cards.anchor: Preserve the bounded outcome: three depth-vial attenuations with normalized spread at most 4 percent at second 120. One stipulated 300 rpm trial already met it after 60 stirring seconds; repeatability and savings relative to the preferred procedure remain unknown.
cards.burden: Two trials per arm provide weak replication. Timing, five-second image transcription, rinsing and reference checks must fit 90 minutes. Report 60 stirring seconds separately from sampling and handling effort; do not infer savings against an unmeasured preferred-rule duration.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: a precommitted mixing dose can reach the final sample target while separating actuation from transient optical spread. Use nominal 300 or 600 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, then remain unstirred until depth sampling starts at second 120. Images are observations with no restart authority.
cards.defeat: Either 300 rpm repeat above 4 percent defeats the claim that both low-speed repeats succeed. Repeated 300 failures with both 600 repeats successful favor an inadequate low-speed dose in this block. Success at both speeds does not establish an optical disturbance mechanism or general sufficiency.
cards.mutation: Replace the 900 rpm optical stopping dependency with a fixed 60-second command; add a 600 rpm comparison to distinguish the tested low-speed dose from stronger rotation.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: both 300 rpm repeats meet the final-vial target despite possible side-image failures, showing repeatable survival of this bounded proxy without sustained 900 rpm or feedback stopping. The 600 rpm arm may also pass.
cards.prediction_rival: Hypothesis: the earlier 300 rpm result was exceptional or sampling-mediated; repeated 300 rpm samples exceed 4 percent, potentially while 600 rpm succeeds. Sampling-order dependence weakens interpretation.
cards.probe: Share one six-trial block with the syringe card: 300, 600, syringe, syringe, 600, 300. Fresh 150 mL water plus 0.30 mL dye in each rinsed beaker; one bottle, locked camera, fixed addition location and common references. Use spill tray; stop on liquid escape. Record five-second side spread, raw frames, depression and specks. Stop operations at second 60. At second 120 withdraw 1 mL from 10, 28 and 45 mm within ten seconds, reversing depth order within each arm. Compute final spread from raw vial attenuation, log failures, actual cessation and effort; no rescue stirring.
cards.rival: Genuine depth gradients require more effective redistribution than the fixed 300 rpm dose, rather than merely changing the optical stopping interface.
unknowns: Nominal rpm lacks independent verification; common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration.
Speck identity and disturbance causation remain unresolved; no matched preferred-rule final samples are supplied.
Sampling can disturb gradients; trial order and the 60-second quiet interval constrain causal attribution.
Other recipes, viscosities, vessel sizes and continuous processes remain untested.

cards.anchor: Hypothetically obtain the same three-depth sample proxy, spread at most 4 percent at second 120, with zero rotational stirring seconds. This values an alternative operating route while keeping manual transfer effort visible.
cards.burden: Four manual 20 mL transfers per syringe trial replace rotational effort, without implying lower total labor. Maintain marked positions and timing without splashing. These trials occupy the two syringe slots in the shared six-trial block, requiring no additional trials or unavailable instruments.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: directed low-to-high bulk transfers redistribute dye sufficiently without rotation. With the stirrer off throughout, withdraw 20 mL at the marked low position and return it at the marked upper side, completing four transfers at seconds 15, 30, 45 and 60. Stop transfers at 60; sample at 120.
cards.defeat: Either syringe repeat above 4 percent defeats the prediction that both pass. Both syringe failures with successful rotational arms reject this transfer schedule as an adequate replacement in this block. Universal failure or strong order dependence leaves the proposed mechanism unresolved.
cards.mutation: Substitute the available syringe bulk-redistribution operation for rotation while retaining the recipe, deadline and independent final-vial outcome. Keep image measurements outside operational control.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: both syringe trials meet the final-vial target with zero stirring seconds, even if transient side images exceed 4 percent. This would support this specific directed-transfer schedule as a feasible alternative, without proving full-volume homogeneity.
cards.prediction_rival: Hypothesis: transfers recycle limited paths or leave unsampled gradients; both syringe trials exceed 4 percent while one or both rotational arms reliably pass. Passing vials alone still cannot exclude gradients outside sampled depths.
cards.probe: Use syringe slots three and four of the shared 300, 600, syringe, syringe, 600, 300 block. Apply the same fresh recipe, references, locked camera, fixed addition location, spill tray and escape stop. Record every transfer, position, cessation time and effort plus five-second images. Sample 10, 28 and 45 mm at second 120 within ten seconds, reversing sampling order between syringe repeats. Compare raw vials, final spreads and all failures with the rotation arms; add no rescue operation.
cards.rival: Directed transfers fail to redistribute dye across the relevant depths adequately; rotation supplies necessary redistribution for this particular comparison.
unknowns: Repeated transfers may revisit the same liquid; 80 mL moved is not 80 mL of distinct volume.
No supplied observation establishes syringe success; transfer-induced gradients and sample disturbance remain possible.
Two adjacent syringe trials give limited protection against drift despite common references and reversed sampling order.
Proxy success cannot establish absolute concentration, uniformity everywhere, or benefits outside this synthetic exercise.
